- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 2-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; use 3–5 day sentiment average to dampen volatility in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
